newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican troops seize six suspected EPR rebels.
newsitem.headline: Mexican troops seize six suspected EPR rebels.

text.p: Troops and police on Wednesday arrested six suspected members of the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) in a remote mountain region in connection with rebel attacks in southern Mexico last month.

A human rights group in close contact with the indigenous village of San Agustin Loxicha, some 50 miles (80 kms) south of Oaxaca, said at least 800 troops poured into the village early on Wednesday, searching homes and carrying out the arrests.
Angelica Ayala, head of the Mexican League for the Defence of Human Rights in the state, told Reuters the troops were guided by four masked men who pointed out the suspects.
EPR guerrillas attacked soldiers and police in the coastal village of La Crucesita, and in Tlaxiaco, in the centre of Oaxaca, on Aug. 28 and about 20 people were killed in the clashes.

Two of those detained on Wednesday were seized on murder and terrorism charges linked to the Aug. 28 attacks, including Fortino Enriquez Hernandez, deputy mayor of San Augustin Loxicha. Four others were held on weapons charges.

"The state Attorney General's Office carried out a joint operation (with police and the army)...and there were detentions of presumed members of the EPR who took part in the attacks in the village of La Crucesita (Oaxaca)," a statement by the government of the southern state of Oaxaca said.
The statement said San Agustin Loxicha because a focus of investigation after a dead guerrilla left behind in the La Crucesita assault was identified as the village's treasurer.

Village residents had complained of military harrasment since the August attacks, and 37 of them were briefly detained by the state government in early September during a protest march to the state capital, Oaxaca.
